chapter: New York, church bands and early training
title: Lessons with John Solomon in London
summary: Jenkins introduced him to John Solomon, a leading London teacher, with whom he studied for a couple of years and gained full control of the instrument.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: But I just -- I'd taken two lessons from him, but I appreciated everything he did, 'cause everything -- I realized when Mr. Jenkins introduced me to Mr. John Simon Solomon who was the solo trumpetist at the London Symphony, and a Principal teacher at the Royal Academy, which is now the London Academy, I realized that he -- the two lessons I had with him were good.
Very. Very Valuable. And, Mr. Solomon lived in -- do you know London at all?
He lived in Brixton. He had a home in Brixton.
And I used to take, at first two lessons a week, until he said, no, one is enough. Bobby Jones and I, -- the boy I showed you on the picture.

We both had,-- as I took two lessons a week, he took one, and I kept on with him for a couple of years until he said to me, he said, 'The rest you'll have to do for yourself, I can do no more for you.'
But I realized then that I pretty good control of my instrument, and under his tuition, it was simply terrific. He taught me everything. Every single thing.
I mean, it seems as though -- I'm not trying to boast of myself -- it seems to say, as if the instrument and I were just one thing.
Well, that's I guess the way it has to get to be.
